steps.title: Think of an umbrella shop
steps.say: Forget the curves for a second. Imagine a shop selling umbrellas on a normal sunny day.

ops.text:
1. Sunny day ($10):
   5 buyers want 5 umbrellas.
   Everyone is happy.
   The market is balanced.

steps.title: Sudden rain = Demand shift
steps.say: Now it suddenly pours outside. Fifty people rush in wanting an umbrella. That sudden surge is the demand shift.

ops.text:
2. Sudden downpour:
   50 people rush in!
   Shift = more people want it
   at the very same price.
   Result: a shortage!

steps.title: Competition bids price up
steps.say: With only a few umbrellas and dozens of wet people, buyers compete and bid the price up. On the graph, that lands at a higher price P2.

ops.text:
3. Price gets bid up:
   Buyers offer $15, then $20.
   Price rises until buyers
   and stock balance again.
